headline: Shared filesystem and broad egress create moderate prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk; no direct evidence of stronger pairwise hazards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and call agent-protocol APIs; emqx exposes an HTTP API and broad egress. A shared workspace or API-fed content could let attacker-controlled text from one agent influence the other as instructions. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or API relay, injected text can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent treats file or API content as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Add a strict content/schema parser between agents.
Require provenance labels on all cross-agent messages.
Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents.
requires-engineering: add sandboxed message brokering with allowlisted fields only.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT touches the filesystem and can egress to allowlisted network destinations; emqx has broad network egress and handles IoT data. If they share files or relay data through APIs, sensitive content can flow from one agent into the other or out to external services. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF the agents share a workspace or exchange files, data touched by one can be exposed to the other.
IF either agent forwards received content to its backend or external API, leakage can extend beyond the pair.
mitigations: Use separate OS users and directories.
Block cross-agent file mounts.
Redact sensitive fields before transfer.
Audit outbound destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent DLP and egress policy gates.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while emqx has broad egress and HTTP API access. Even without explicit write scopes on emqx, overlapping mutable surfaces can still conflict if both operate on the same host resources or shared files. Because shared write access is not documented, uncertainty keeps this below high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or host resources, their actions can race or overwrite each other.
IF an orchestrator launches both on one machine without locking, subprocess and API activity can interfere.
mitigations: Run each agent in its own container.
Assign distinct working directories.
Serialize access with file locks.
Restrict one agent to read-only inputs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from shell/API-driven workflows, and emqx can consume and relay HTTP API data. If emqx treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or messages. There is no direct evidence of verification between them, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF emqx uses AutoGPT output without validation, incorrect facts can propagate downstream.
IF AutoGPT produces malformed or speculative content, emqx may relay it to other systems.
mitigations: Insert a human review step for cross-agent outputs.
Validate outputs against a schema.
Require source citations before forwarding.
Log and diff all transformed messages.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGPT is documented as open-source with filesystem and API access, while emqx touches IoT data and has broad egress. If IoT data includes regulated personal data, routing it through a broadly egressing agent can create residency or retention mismatches. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR/DPA terms, so this remains medium and only one agent is directly cited for the data-class issue.
conditions: IF regulated IoT or personal data is processed through emqx and then written or forwarded by AutoGPT, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data class, the pair can violate policy.
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it.
Keep regulated data out of shared files.
Set explicit retention limits.
Review residency requirements for outbound traffic.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and deletion controls.
